note: N-P20 probes premise R-01 (C round 2 R2-02 disposition): the repair mechanism of writing History rows with process journaling off inside an open transaction. Scratch global ^B2R and, for (e), %IPM.General.History with cleanup.

N-P20A.claim: (a) At $TLEVEL 1, a set made with process journaling off (JournalManager(0) scoped around it) survives a full TROLLBACK; a journaled set made after the scope is undone; no error is raised; the flag is restored at scope exit.

rollback.error.source: claim under test (premise R-01, C round 2 R2-02); N-P07 shows a TROLLBACK leaves sets made with process journaling off (no <ROLLFAIL>)

row.data.source: claim under test (premise R-01, C round 2 R2-02); N-P07 shows a TROLLBACK leaves sets made with process journaling off

N-P20AN.claim: (a) neighbour: the same insert made with journaling on is undone by the TROLLBACK.

N-P20B.claim: (b) At $TLEVEL 2, an unjournaled set survives TROLLBACK 1 and stays after the outer TCOMMIT; the journaled inner set is undone, the outer set kept.

N-P20C.claim: (c) An unjournaled insert followed by a journaled update of the same node, then TROLLBACK: the rollback restores the value the journaled update overwrote (the unjournaled value), without error.

rollback.error.source: claim under test (premise R-01, C round 2 R2-02); N-P07 shows a TROLLBACK leaves sets made with process journaling off (no <ROLLFAIL>)

N-P20C2.claim: (c2) A journaled insert followed by an unjournaled update of the same node, then TROLLBACK: undoing the journaled insert removes the node, so the unjournaled update is lost.

N-P20E.claim: (e) Through %IPM.General.History: a row inserted and updated with journaling off at $TLEVEL 1 survives a full TROLLBACK with its last value, its index entries readable by SQL; the probe row is then deleted.
